requirements.text: A TownCentreZone component exists that reports, each frame, whether any living Russian infantry soldier is inside the town centre and whether any living Ukrainian soldier is inside it, using UnitRegistry alive-soldier queries.

A centreTimer field counts up only while Russian infantry is inside the zone and no living Ukrainian soldier is inside; it resets to zero as soon as a Ukrainian soldier is inside or no Russian infantry remains. The hold duration is 60 seconds, defined as a named constant or configurable field.

The CountdownHud class is a MonoBehaviour that writes the remaining seconds (hold duration minus centreTimer) to a TextMeshProUGUI label, and the label is visible only while the timer is running and hidden when it is reset.
When centreTimer reaches 60 s the zone raises an OnCentreHeld event exactly once, and the day-loss logic (BattleEndChecker) subscribes to it to record a 'centre held' day-lost outcome.
CountdownHud is hooked into the running game: it is created or added to the battle HUD (e.g. in HudFrame or MainHudUI) in a file other than CountdownHud.cs.
An EditMode or PlayMode test exercises the countdown: it asserts the timer advances with Russian infantry alone in the zone, resets when a Ukrainian soldier enters, and fires OnCentreHeld after 60 s.

The previous try failed because PlayMode ran zero tests, not because of a compile error. The harness ran PlayMode with `-testFilter CountdownHud`, which matches on test names. The only test was `TownCentreHoldTest.CentreTimer_AdvancesAlone_…`, which doesn't contain "CountdownHud", so nothing was selected.

I haven't run Unity, so the new test hasn't been compiled or run yet.

**Changed this time**
- `ELVATR GAME 1/Assets/Tests/PlayMode/TownCentreHoldTest.cs`: added a second test, `CountdownHud_ShowsRemainingSeconds_HidesOnReset_AndAfterOnCentreHeld`, so the `CountdownHud` filter now finds a test. It builds the countdown on a test canvas and checks that:
  - the label is hidden when nobody is in the centre;
  - it shows "55" after 5 s of Russian infantry alone;
  - it hides when a Ukrainian soldier resets the timer;
  - `OnCentreHeld` fires once at 60 s, and the label is hidden after that.

**From the previous try, unchanged**
- `Scripts/Game/TownCentreZone.cs`: the zone. Each frame it asks `UnitRegistry` for living soldiers on both sides and runs the 60 s `centreTimer`, raising `OnCentreHeld` once.
- `Scripts/Game/BattleEndChecker.TownCentre.cs`: adds the zone, listens for `OnCentreHeld` and records the "centre held" day loss.
- `Scripts/UI/CountdownHud.cs`: the label under the top bar showing the seconds left; hidden while the timer is at zero.
- `Scripts/Game/BattleEndChecker.cs`: marked `partial`, plus one hook-up line.
- `Scripts/Game/FeatureFlags.cs`: new `TownCentreHold` flag, on by default.
- `Scripts/UI/HudFrame.cs`: one line that adds the countdown to the battle HUD when the flag is on.

One thing to watch: `CountdownHud` only uses a `TextMeshProUGUI` label if the "TMP Settings" resource is in the build. Without it, it falls back to the HUD's ordinary text in the pixel font, so it doesn't crash in a standalone build. In that fallback the countdown never uses TextMeshPro.
